chapter: Teachers, Blakey and Miles on music
title: Art Blakey: be an emissary on and off the bandstand
summary: Blakey told musicians not to brag about Philadelphia sandwiches in Paris and not to be arrogant to waiters who may own the club later.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Yeah. “Don’t be... You’re eating in a French restaurant or the hotel or whatever, and keep bragging about how great the subway [sic] sandwich... And about how they treat people. He was talking to someone thick-headed. He said, “you’re still on the bandstand when you’re walking down the street, and when you’re playing...” We played a lot of club concerts then, too. “When you’re playing in a club, don’t be arrogant to the waiters and everything; we’ve got to come back here maybe 15 years from now, and that waiter is going to own the club—he’s going to be the promoter.” So he was always really cool about Europe and Japan.
